subject: [Fircrest] Private cluster throughput regression 1 exec remediation request
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fircresthealth.com
Date: 2026-09-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in inference latency & 503s after config change (private cluster)

Jordan —

We saw a sudden degradation on our private VPC cluster starting at ~07:45 PT this morning. Key symptoms: p95 inference latency jumped from ~600ms to ~2.8s, sustained 503s across the API (~8-12% of requests), and sustained throughput is down roughly 40%. This started immediately after you pushed the runtime config update you mentioned on Friday (runtime v2.14.1).

Attaching a screenshot of the dashboard and a short sample of the error lines from the edge nodes. Our production traffic is critical for appointment confirmation flows  this is impacting users.

As an urgent ask: can you (1) advise a quick mitigation (fallback to prior runtime? disable batching?) and (2) confirm whether Redwood can temporarily expand capacity or fail traffic to hosted inference while we stabilize? Procurement and I will need timeline and any cost/credit details for the account.

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Fircrest Health

Attachments: fircrest_p95_spike.png (image), fircrest_error_sample.log (text)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T08:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference latency & 503s after config change (private cluster)

Anita — thanks for the heads-up and the attachments.

I'm standing up an ops war room now. Connor (runtime on-call) and Marissa (customer success/ops) are looped in. Immediate plan:
- War room in ~30m (09:00 PT)  link to follow.
- Connor: triage runtime change impact + quick rollback feasibility.
- Marissa: evaluate temporary capacity bump and cost/credit implications; coordination with procurement.
- I will also prepare an exec one-pager for our leadership and your stakeholders.

If you can share a short-lived S3/Drive link with the full metrics query (or grant read access), that'll help accelerate root cause.

Jordan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference latency & 503s after config change (private cluster)

Looping my initial findings after 20m triage in the war room:

Summary: the runtime bump (v2.14.1) altered kernel selection heuristics for large-context batches which appears to cause pathological slowdowns under the current batch-size distribution from Fircrest. We see increased mem pressure on the KV cache allocator and contention on the attention kernel path, causing request timeouts that present as 503s.

Quick mitigations (low-risk, ~10-20m to enact for canary, 30-60m for full):
- Roll back to runtime v2.13.7 on a 10% canary shard to validate (command and patch attached: runtime-rollback.patch).
- Lower max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 in the route config to reduce kernel switching overhead.
- Temporarily bump KV cache allocation (config kv_cache_fraction 0.25 -> 0.35) to reduce evictions.
- If rollback is not possible immediately, enable immediate fallback to the L2 model variant (lower context window) to reduce attention compute.

Risk notes: rollback has minimal data risk but will briefly disrupt in-flight KV caches (expect short-lived cold starts). Bumping capacity will incur cost; fallback model will slightly change response characteristics.

Attaching profiler output and kernel profile: kernel-profile.txt and a small rollback patch. I'll start the canary rollback when Jordan approves.

- Connor
Senior Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runtime-rollback.patch (text), kernel-profile.txt (text)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in inference latency & 503s after config change (private cluster)

Updates from ops/CS perspective:
- We can provision 2 additional worker nodes in the Fircrest VPC immediately (30-45m lead time) if they authorize temporary burst capacity. Estimated incremental cost: $2,800/day. We can offer a one-day credit while we stabilize and then reconcile with procurement.
- If Jordan wants an exec escalation to our customer success leadership (for credit approval) I can draft a short memo.
- Connor's rollback + batch-size reduction looks like the fastest path to cut off the 503s. Recommend canary rollback + kv_cache bump now, then evaluate after 45m metrics window before scaling.

I've created Jira FIR-9021 to track the remediation steps and will attach post-mortem artifacts there.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Related: JIRA FIR-9021

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Executive brief (Fircrest)  incident summary and ask

Laura / team  attaching a concise one-pager for leadership: exec-onepager.pdf. TL;DR: runtime v2.14.1 kernel heuristic change caused KV cache churn + attention contention under Fircrest's batch distribution, producing p95 regression and 503s. Action taken: canary rollback to v2.13.7 initiated at 09:40 PT; batch-size lowered; KV cache fraction bumped; monitoring window of 45m.

Ask for leadership: pre-approve a one-day credit for Fircrest (up to $3k) to be applied immediately if rollback does not restore baseline within the monitoring window. Marissa will follow up with the procurement wording.

I will keep Anita and Tom updated; will post post-mortem within 48 hours.

Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: exec-onepager.pdf

From: Anita Rao <anita@fircresthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fircresthealth.com, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@fircresthealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executive brief (Fircrest)  incident summary and ask

Jordan / team —

Thank you for the fast response and the one-pager. Canary rollback restored p95 within ~30min and 503s subsided; throughput is back to ~95% of baseline. We'll hold off on bursting extra nodes for now. Procurement will follow up on the credit memo; they asked for an itemized list of remediation steps and timestamps for reconciliation.

Please include the timeline and final post-mortem (root cause + preventive config guardrails) in JIRA FIR-9021 and to the Drive link provided earlier. Well want a short customer-facing summary for our ops leadership.

Anita Rao
Head of Platform Engineering
Fircrest Health
